lines.en: : Okay, Chinami. I’m putting you in charge of checking the CDs and vinyls. Grab as much as you possibly can now and I’ll be over there to double check after I scour the last of the concert DVDs.
: Then, we’ll triple and quadruple check the store before heading to the next one. Do you understand? Good. Also, ask whoever’s working if they have anything else in the back they might be hiding.
: Oh! Ask about cardboard cutouts and promotional posters too! I know I’ve seen some here before! Leverage your cuteness if you have to!
: Or, if it’s a creepy looking older person, call for me so I can leverage my own assets! Do you copy?!
: Chinami wants boba. Eating sugar packets all morning has led to a dangerous addiction that she must now deal with for the rest of her life.

: Niki first, boba second! I’ll buy you all the boba in the fucking world once we’ve made sure that no one else in Kumon-mi is hoarding the queen’s merch! This is the last chance we’ll ever get and it needs to be taken seriously!

: Okay. Chinami will go check for CDs. But she urges big sis Chika to maybe think a little bit more about what’s happening since she did just find out Papa has been cheating on her with her favorite idol.
: Oh my god. You’re right.
: See?! Big sis Chika’s been going so crazy after meeting Niki that she forgot about what’s really-
: This basically means I’ve kissed her too! Among other things! SO MANY OTHER THINGS. Oh my god. Oh my god, oh my god, oh my god. I shouldn’t feel this way in public, BUT I DO!
: Hah...okay. Chinami will take on her mission for real now...
: But only because she really wants boba and-
: Hm?
: Nao-chan? Big sis Chika, Nao-chan is here.
: Good! That means more hands! Get her to help too! OH, TSUKASA! CALL TSUKASA! WE NEED MORE MONEY!
: Nao-chan! Would you like to come help the Chosokabes check the store for-
: Now, Chinami is sad. Nao-chan left.
: Then go get her! It’ll be worth the time investment when we can leverage her cuteness too! I’ll be fine here! Go, Chinami! Go, go, go!!!
: Fine! Jeez Louise, big sis Chika! It’s like Chinami’s the older sister all of a sudden and she’s just not ready for that!
: YOU THERE! EMPLOYEE GIRL! I know you’re hiding things from me. LET ME IN THE BACK ROOM! NOW!
: Nao-chan, would you like to get boba with Chinami while her big sister has an episode in the music store? Chinami doesn’t have any money, but she learned something about using her assets to-
: What? A magical portal? Really?
: Two magical portals? But what are they doing in the mall? Was that part of the renovation project that kept Chinami from experiencing commerce for such a long period of time?

: You don’t have to tell Chinami that. She understands better than anyone that capitalism is just one more means to an end. But that doesn’t mean Chinami isn’t going to participate in it since failure to conform would only lead to a further accelerated gap in class and status.
: Of course Chinami already set up a Roth IRA. What kind of fool do you take her for?
“And so a few mortals encountered two portals,” he chortled so heartily it sounded aortal.

One to death, one to life. One so welcoming, hell’s coming, go get your wife (then replace her piece by piece until she’s a new wife and it sparks a debate on what percentage of person a person can be until adultery becomes childtery.) JOKE.
: Chinami is confused and bemused in determining which portal is the one we should use.
: Really? But if they aren’t safe, why did somebody put them in the middle of the mall?
: Chinami can read! But she’s concerned this could be one more example of false advertising since the “Death” portal looks so warm and welcoming.
: Huh. That’s an interesting way to look at it, and one that helps Chinami better cope with the fact that she will one day be among the sunflowers.
: She thinks she’s going to go through the “Life” portal, though. Even if it seems a little scarier than the other one. Because life is objectively better than death.
: Together then? Should we maybe tie a string to something here so we can find our way back?
: Okay! Chinami is confident that Nao-chan knows the way, so she will follow her lead. We need to be quick, though! Big sis Chika will get mad at Chinami if she doesn’t help fuel her obsession.
One step, two steps, three steps, jump.
What fun we will have once the tree is a stump.
: No, you guys aren’t listening! I’m telling you that’s not the way it is!
: You’ve been telling us that’s not the way it is for like ten minutes now, dude.
: But if literally everyone in the room is apparently “misunderstanding” you, I’m just saying it’s possible that maybe you’re the one who’s not really “getting it.”
: Hailey’s right, Paul. Like, we get that she’s in heat and everything, but that doesn’t mean you can say things that...forward and expect to get away with it.
: It wasn’t forward at all, bro! She’s like a sister to me! You guys are just misunderstanding the context. Besides, there’s already some other girl I like. I wouldn’t-
: What, you mean Hailey?
: You- what?! No!
: Aww, Paul. That’s cute. It’d be cuter if you weren’t such an asshole, sure. But I’m glad that your heart is at least functional enough to have feelings for somebody at the end of the day.
: My heart is perfectly functional!
: Care to weigh in Octavia? You’ve got three hearts, don’t you?
: Yeah, and four boyfriends. Why does she need to weigh in at all?
: We broke up like a year ago, Paul. Get over it already. But yes, as the one person here who’s been unfortunate enough to actually date this guy, I can confirm that he does have feelings. Sometimes.
: Sometimes?! When did I ever-
: Wait, Paul. Hold on.
: Hey! You over there. Are you new here?
: Yeah! What are you just standing around for? Come hang out with us. We won’t bite.
: Unless you want us to.
: See, this is exactly why everyone’s always talking shit on you. There’s no way that girl’s even sexually mature yet.
: She’s a dog, isn’t she? Don’t they hit sexual maturity at, like...six months sometimes?
: You think that’s impressive? Bees hit it at six days. Hi, new girl! I’m Beatrice! Tell us your name and body count!
: My...body count? What does...that mean?
: Ignore them. Come chat! We’re just getting ready for the Transpacific Sadness Symposium in a few years. There’s no need to be shy!
: There goes Hailey jumping at the first chance she gets to flirt with a dog again.
: Oh, right. Lamar is here. Thank you for chiming in, Lamar. Your opinion was both needed and wanted.
: He’s got a point though, Hailey. You do have a type.
: I do not! I just remember when I was new and Howard was always going out of his way to include me in stuff. Feeling left out sucks. We can all agree on that, right?
: Dogs, Hailey? Really?
: It’s the 21st century, Paul. Try checking your bigotry at the door next party.
: Octavia fucked a dog once.
: It was a lot more than once.
: Uh...actually, I...I don’t think I’m supposed to be here...
: I need to be...helping my sister with something...
: You have a sister? Is it just one? I have thirteen. Come talk! I want to get to know you.
: Oh, here we go again. Manic pixie Hailey is back in action to swipe some newcomer off her feet.
: Seriously, Lamar. Shut up. You barely know me.
: So...your name is Hailey?
: Hailey Hawthorne. I’m from Michigan. What about you? What’s your name? What’s your story?
: Chinami Chosokabe. I’m from Kumon-mi.
: Kumon-mi? Is that in Massachusetts or something?
: I’m pretty sure that’s Japan, actually. Kumon-mi’s that city they blocked off from the rest of the world during that extremely isolated space war a few years back.
: Oh my god, Japan? That’s so far! When did you get to America? Are you here for long or what?
: I don’t know. I went through a portal in the mall with my friend Nao-chan and suddenly I was here. Do you know how to get back?
: I think you’d need to buy a plane ticket. Are planes even going to that Kumon-mi place if they’re blocked off, though?
: Octavia, you’re the smart one here. Do you know if there’s another one of those portal things Chinami could take back home after the party? You are staying for the party. Right, Chinami?
: I’m not really supposed to go to parties. I get sick really easily and big sis Chika says they’re a breeding ground for germs.
: Do you not get out much then?
: Basically never. I’m not even allowed to go to school. I just sit at home all day and watch TV.
: Wait, so is this your first party ever? Do you drink? I can show you where the cooler is.
: Do you have apple juice? I’m addicted to sugar now.
: Howard should. He’s an addict too. Are you sure you need that, though? You’re so young. You’re going to ruin your skin.
: I can call someone if you’re serious. Not here, though. And you didn’t hear that from me.
: On second thought, Chinami should probably-
: Mm!
: Hm? Something wrong?
: Did you just accidentally speak in the third person? Oh my god, that’s precious! I love her.
: I...have a bad habit of doing that sometimes...I’m sorry.
: Why are you apologizing? Just be yourself, Chinami. Hailey thinks that’s the cool thing to do.
: It’s just...a little embarrassing. Ch...I’ve never been around cool, older kids before. All of my big sister’s friends are kind of lame and weird.
: You think we’re cool? Really?
: Don’t get too excited. Dogs love everybody.
: Especially Octavia.
: You should try one too, Beatrice. I know this German shepherd who’s really into bugs. I could give you his number if you want.
: I don’t know...Like, don’t get me wrong, it sounds hot. But look at me. I’m probably like...one twentieth of his size.
: Well, duh. Why do you think he’s into bugs in the first place?
: Oh. So he’s one of those.
: You haven’t answered my question yet. You really think we’re cool?
: Chinami learned from TV that parties are for cool kids normally. Is that not true?
: You did the thing again.
: Paul, shh. Leave her alone. This is basically a brand new world for Chinami. Who cares how she speaks?
: Thank you, Hailey. I really do need to leave, though. My sister’s going to be really mad that I left her at the mall.
: Assuming she even remembers I exist right now and it isn’t too busy shopping...
: Well hey, one little sister to another, I’ve learned to accept that we’re not always going to be the top priority. Everybody needs space sometimes. Even family.
: Besides, it’s too late to get a plane ticket out of here. I can drive you to the airport in the morning if you want. And you can crash at my place in the meantime. It’s nearby.
: Is there really no portal back to Japan? Because I’m worried about Nao-chan too. She can’t speak and it might be harder for her to make friends. Nobody is gonna drive her to the airport.
: Is Nao-chan your...girlfriend? Or just a regular friend who also happens to be a girl?
: She’s just a friend. I don’t really know anything about romance and stuff.
: Maybe it’s different here, but I’m still kind of young where I’m from.
: Told you she wasn’t sexually mature yet. Always trust the octopus.
: Tell you what! How about you and I step outside to get some air and escape from all the noise? I can help you look around for one of those portal things.
: And, in the unfortunate event that we’re unable to find one, we can figure out where to go from there.

: Worst case scenario, I give you a ride to the airport in the morning. And, if it helps you avoid getting in trouble, you can just tell your sister I kidnapped you or something. I don’t mind if she hates me.
: Big sis Chika wouldn’t hate you. If anything, she’d be really happy that you helped me. She’s awesome! And maybe, if the portal is still here, she can come to your next party too?
: Yeah! The more, the merrier. I can bring one of my sisters too so she can have a date. We’ll make a whole thing out of it.
: Hailey-
: Don’t even think about it, Paul. Nobody likes a cockblock.
: Again, ignore them. Just come with me so everybody can stop interrupting us. Portal-hunt, go!
: Portal-hunt, go!
: You might have to tell me what they look like, though. I’ve never seen a portal in person before.
: Neither had Chinami until- mm!
: Hahahaha! You don’t need to stop yourself, Chinami! It’s totally fine. And like, totally adorable too.
: Hah...
: Look at him sighing as if he ever had a chance with her in the first place.
: Yeah, this was done and dusted the second Hailey found out she wasn’t from around here. Exactly her type too.
: What, young and oblivious?
: I’d say inexperienced is more politically correct. But yeah, pretty much.
: I don’t know. Hailey seemed different this time. Maybe she actually likes her?
: You say that every time, don’t you?
: Yeah, and I’m usually right. It’s not my fault she subsequently stops liking them shortly afterward.
: She probably gets it from you.
: Seriously, Paul. Just get the fuck over me already.
: Sorry we couldn’t find one of those portals, Chinami. Can you maybe just call your sister and explain what’s going on?
: My phone doesn’t get any service here. International roaming plans don’t make much sense when your city is closed off from the rest of the world.
: Yeah, I can imagine. I hope you’re able to get back safe. I don’t really know the situation over there.
: Do you like living in Japan? I’ve always wanted to see Mt. Fuji. What’s it like in person?
: I’ve actually never seen it. But maybe when the walls are down one day, I can take a trip there and take some pictures.
: With your friend, Nao-chan?
: I have other friends too. Well, one other friend. Her name is Tsukasa and she’s super rich.
: Aww, just one other friend? Have I not made the cut?
: I like you too, Hailey. But why would you even want to be friends with somebody like me? I live so far away and we might not ever see each other again.
: Hahah, yeah. I guess you’re right about that. I don’t really know, though. Like, I’m just...I don’t know. You’re interesting. I don’t talk to dogs much.
: I get it. I don’t talk to rabbits much. You’re the first one, actually.
: I’ve got some bad news then.
: It’s not about the World Trade Center, is it?
: No. Just that I’m not actually a rabbit. I’m a hare.
: Oh, really? I hope I didn’t offend you. I don’t really know the difference between those two things.
: It’s totally fine, hahah! Not many people do. But hares have longer ears and legs and are basically just, like...bigger, cooler rabbits.
: Really, the only thing rabbits have on us is their sex drive. They reproduce like way more often since their gestation period is like 50%% faster or something like that.
: Can you even imagine? Like, you have sex one time and boom. Thirty days later, you’ve got like ten kits hopping around.
: No wonder you have so many sisters.
: You can borrow some if you’d like. I have more than enough to share.
: I’m happy with the sister I have. She can just be a little crazy sometimes.
: Really? How so?
: Just boy stuff mostly. She was fine until she fell in love. Now, she’s always freaking out about romance for a bunch of different reasons I don’t really understand.
: Yeah, romance will do that to a person. My oldest sister was the same when she met her husband. And now they’re talking about having kids of their own, so I’m sure she’ll get even crazier.
: Do you have a boyfriend, Hailey? You seem too cool to not have one. Maybe you can give my big sister some tips on how to stay that way?
: Hm? No, I don’t have a boyfriend. I’m a lesbian.
: Well...I guess I’m bisexual technically. But I’ve only ever dated girls before. It’s just easier, you know?
: Easier? How so?
: Well, I don’t ever have to worry about suddenly having kids. So that’s a plus.
: But there’s just something inherently easier about dating another you, I think. Especially if they’re around the same age and use the same makeup and stuff.
: Do hares even use makeup?
: Of course we do. Just look at my eyeliner. Now, imagine a world where that eyeliner belongs to an ex and you didn’t even have to pay for it. Kablam. You just saved five dollars.
: It’s kind of hard to see in the dark.
: Here, get a closer look. Can you see it now? Do you bear witness to my sexually-driven frugality?
: Oh, okay. Chinami can see it now. She thinks saving money on eyeliner is a strange reason to like girls, though.
: Well, it’s obviously not just that. It’s just...I don’t know. I’ve always been attracted to girls.
: It’s hard to keep my heart steady when I encounter somebody I find pretty. And I’m not only saying that because my resting heart rate is like three times the speed of a dog’s.
: Do you get what I’m saying, though? Like, have you ever met anybody who makes your heart beat faster?
: Not yet. But Chinami hasn’t met many people at all yet, so she’s not even sure what kind of person she likes.
: How about this Nao-chan girl?
: But Chinami already said that Nao-chan is just a friend.
: Sure. But you can be friends with somebody and still want to be with them. You know what I mean?
: Like you and me for example. If we kissed right now, it’s not like we’d just graduate from being friends all of a sudden. We’d just be...you know. Acting on an impulse.
: Chinami doesn’t know how to kiss, though. So she thinks you’d probably start hating her and not want to be her friend anymore.
: You’re pretty much exclusively stuck in third person now. Can I take that as you being more comfortable with me?
: Mhm! Chinami knows you don’t want to hurt her and won’t make fun of her, so she doesn’t mind if she makes speaking mistakes now.
: Don’t call them mistakes. They’re impulses. Just wanting to do something doesn’t automatically make it wrong. Especially if it’s something small like a name.
: Or a kiss?
: Exactly.
: Chinami thinks she understands now. And she’s glad she has somebody like Hailey to teach her.
: And Hailey’s glad she has somebody like Chinami to make her feel a little less alone.
: Mm...you’re really warm. And soft...
: Do you ever get scared, Chinami?
: Of what?
: This.
: Getting close to someone you know you shouldn’t. The paths your mind leads you down that you know are wrong, but there’s just something so...exciting and new about it.
: Chinami has a friend who keeps trying to show her exciting and new things too. But all they really do is make Chinami nervous.
: What kind of things?
: Things that even Chinami’s older sister doesn’t want to teach her about.
: Like things that adults do?
: Mhm. And that is kind of scary, so she thinks she understands what you’re trying to say.
: You know...
: The best way to stop being scared of something is to face it head on.
: Head on?...
: Mhm...
: Like, for example, kissing is probably really scary to you right now since you’ve never done it before. But it’d be a lot less scary if you understood that it was safe, right?
: I guess so...That makes sense.
: Then...
: Maybe you’d want to practice with me?
: Sorry! Sorry. That was stupid. Of course you wouldn’t want to practice with me. Like, what am I even saying? Hahahah!
: Nobody’s ever wanted to kiss Chinami before. She’s not sure how to respond.
: Well...
: Does Chinami want to kiss Hailey? Just to...you know...see what it’s like?
: Unless you already know that you don’t like girls at all, which is totally fair. Like, I’m not trying to pressure you or anything. I just...yeah.
: I want to kiss you.
: Your mouth. Your neck. Your hands. Everywhere. I have since the moment I saw you. And I’m sorry for keeping that a secret, but-
: Okay.
: O...Okay?
: You can kiss Chinami.
: But only for a little while, okay?
: And only because you made her heart beat really fast just now.
: Okay...
: Eyes...closed? Or open? Closed helps with the nerves.
: Chinami will close her eyes then...But also! You need to keep this a secret from her big sister! Chinami thinks she’d get in trouble if she found out she kissed a hare.
: Yeah, don’t worry. I’ve had plenty of girls tell me the exact same thing.
: Be calm, okay?...
: I’ll start slow...
: But...
: Please forgive me if I can’t control myself after a few seconds.
: N...Nao-chan?!
: YOU THERE! EMPLOYEE GIRL! I know you’re hiding things from me. LET ME IN THE BACK ROOM! NOW!
: What do you mean it’s for employees only?! If I have to get a job here, I will! Where’s the fucking manager?! WHERE?!
: Fine! Call the fucking police! See if they can stop me! See if- AAAH! YOU! LITTLE GIRL! GET THE FUCK AWAY FROM THAT BOX SET! THAT’S MINE!
